transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm in the right place. It's probably just a small thing, maybe just me having a bit too much energy for a guy my age. 

But... well, when I'm supposed to sit still—like during our maintenance staff meetings at work, or briefings for church events—I just get this feeling. It's almost like I’ve got a motor humming right under my skin. I try really hard to be polite and not bother anyone, I promise. But I usually end up shifting around in my seat a lot, or I'll stand up in the back, or just find some little excuse to move around. I hope that makes sense? Is that... is that the sort of thing you see people for?

When did you first notice this feeling of having to move around or this difficulty sitting still? Has it been something you've dealt with since you were a child, or is it something that's come up more recently?

Well, um... I guess it's actually been around for a long time. Since I was a kid, really. I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker, because I really always tried to be a good boy, I promise. But... yeah, I do remember getting scolded a bit back in grade school. 

I'd end up popping out of my seat, or I'd accidentally talk over the teacher... or I'd just rush ahead on things before she even finished giving the directions. I never meant to be disrespectful to anyone, I just... I don't know, I'd get a little too eager, I suppose? My mother, bless her heart, she used to say I acted like I was wound just a little too tight, even back then. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

Beyond the difficulty sitting still and the rushing ahead, do you find it hard to concentrate or keep your attention on tasks? For example, do you have trouble focusing during conversations, or do your thoughts tend to jump around a lot?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I have a problem with that. I'm a good listener, I really am. I always try to pay attention when people are talking to me, especially at work or at church. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was ignoring them. 

Sometimes... maybe if a meeting goes on for a really, really long time, my mind might wander just a tiny bit, but I think that happens to everyone, right? I can usually snap right back to it. I don't think my thoughts jump around or anything like that. I'm pretty good at staying on track with my cleaning duties, too. I just... I just like to get things done quickly, you know? 

I hope that answers your question? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just don't think I have much trouble with the focusing part. Is that okay?

You mentioned rushing ahead before instructions are finished—do you find yourself making quick decisions or doing things impulsively without thinking through the consequences first, or is it mainly just the physical restlessness and rushing to finish tasks?

Well, I wouldn't say I do things without thinking, exactly. I really try to be careful and do a good job. But... well, I suppose I do have a habit of jumping the gun just a little bit when people are talking to me. 

Like, if my supervisor at work or one of the staff at church is explaining something they need me to do... I just want to show them I understand, you know? So I might, um, jump in and finish their sentence or say what I think they're going to ask before they're quite done. I just want to be helpful and get right to it! 

But, I admit, sometimes I guess wrong about what they were going to say, and then they have to stop and correct me. I always feel terrible when that happens, I really do. I don't mean to interrupt them or act like a know-it-all. It's just... I get so eager to help out. 

Is that the kind of thing you mean, Doctor? I hope I'm not making myself sound too difficult to work with.

You mentioned interrupting people and rushing to finish tasks—have there been times in your life when you've made decisions quickly that you later regretted? For example, with money, or saying something to someone that you wished you hadn't said right away?

Oh... oh, goodness, no. I really don't think I do that. I mean, with money, I've always been very, very careful. Working as a building cleaner, you know, I have to watch my budget pretty closely, so I never really go out and just buy things on a whim. I'd hate to be irresponsible like that. 

And, um... as for saying things I shouldn't? I really try my absolute best to be polite to everyone. I might accidentally interrupt, like I was saying before, but it's never anything mean or... or thoughtless, I promise. I'd feel just awful if I ever hurt someone's feelings by blurting something out. I always want to make sure people feel respected, whether it's the folks at my church or the people whose offices I clean. 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers... I just don't think I have much trouble with those kinds of big decisions. Is it okay that I don't have that problem?

You've mentioned you like to move around and get things done quickly, but I'm curious—in your daily life, do you find yourself doing things without planning ahead? For instance, have there been times when you acted on something right away and then realized you should have thought about it first?

Oh, um... well, no, I don't really think I do that. I actually try to be very careful about planning my day out. Especially with my job, you know? I have a set routine for cleaning the different floors, and I like to stick to it so I don't miss a single spot. I'd just hate to do a bad job and disappoint the building manager. 

So, even though I like to work fast and stay busy, it's usually just me following the plan I already made in my head. I don't really jump into things blindly or... or do things without thinking them through first. I'd be so worried about causing a problem or making extra work for someone else if I did that. 

I try really, really hard to be dependable. I hope it's okay that I don't have that issue? I know you have to ask all these questions, and I want to be helpful for your assessment... I just honestly try my absolute best to be responsible. Does that sound alright to you?

You mentioned interrupting people sometimes—do you find that you talk a lot, or that once you get going, it's hard to stop talking? Do people ever comment that you talk more than others, or that you talk really fast?

Oh, gosh, no... I really don't think I'm like that. I actually try to be pretty quiet, especially at work. You know, when you're cleaning offices, people are busy, and the last thing I'd want to do is bother them by talking their ear off. I'd be so embarrassed if someone thought I was being a nuisance like that. 

I mean, I'll say a polite hello, of course, and ask how their day is going! But I don't think anyone has ever told me I talk too much, or too fast. I really try my best to be a good listener instead. 

I hope that's okay? I know you're looking for certain things with these questions, but I just... I really try to be respectful of other people's peace and quiet. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm not messing up your assessment by not having that problem.

You've told me about feeling restless during meetings at work and church. Outside of those situations where you have to sit still, like when you're at home relaxing or doing activities you enjoy, do you still feel that motor-like sensation you described, or does it mainly happen when you're supposed to be sitting in one place?

Oh, um... well, I suppose even when I'm just trying to relax, I might still be a little bit... busy? I really try to just settle down, I promise I do. Like when my wife and I go fishing, or if we're sitting through a game of bingo. I want to just be quiet and enjoy the evening with her, I truly do. 

But... well, I'll catch myself tapping, or maybe talking a bit too loud without meaning to. Or I'll just keep messing and messing with my tackle box, or fiddling with the bingo pencil. It just gets a little hard for me to just be completely quiet and enjoy it like she does. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bother to be around. I always try to catch myself so I don't ruin her good time. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm answering your question right... I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

When you're doing activities that you find really interesting or enjoyable—like hobbies you love, or things that keep you engaged—do you still feel that same restless, motor-like sensation, or does it seem to go away when you're doing something you're really into?

Oh, um... well, when I'm doing something I really love... I think I'm actually pretty good at just focusing on it. Like, if I'm fixing something around the house or... or doing a puzzle, I try really hard to just settle into it. I wouldn't say I feel that same antsy feeling then. 

I mean, I might still be moving my hands or shifting around a little, but I don't feel like a motor is running inside me or anything like that. I really try to just enjoy the moment, especially if it's something nice. I wouldn't want to ruin a good hobby by being all keyed up, you know? 

So, I think... I think it mostly goes away when I'm really interested in something. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I am. I really do try my best to be calm when I'm supposed to be having fun. Is that helpful for your notes, Doctor?

When you're at home in the evenings, or just going about your day on weekends when there's no particular schedule you have to follow, do you still feel that restless, motor-like sensation most of the time, or is it mainly just when you're in those situations where you're supposed to sit still, like at meetings?

Oh, well... I guess even when I don't have to be on a schedule, I do still like to keep pretty busy. I hope that's not a bad thing! I just... I always try to be useful, I suppose. 

Like, on my shifts at work, I go right from mopping to checking the trash to straightening up the chairs without really stopping. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and keeping the place nice for everyone. And then, well, even when I get home after work... instead of just sitting down and putting my feet up, I'll usually end up out in the garage. I'll start puttering around out there, or maybe re-sorting my tools and things. 

I just prefer to keep moving and getting things done. I wouldn't want my wife to think I'm just lazing around the house, you know? So I guess I am always kind of on the go, even on the weekends when I could be resting. I don't really feel that antsy feeling as much if I'm just being productive. 

Is that what you were asking, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it right for your assessment. I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.

When you're doing something at home that you really enjoy and find absorbing—like a hobby or project you're passionate about—do you still get that motor-like restless feeling, or does it completely go away?

Oh, um... well, I think it's kind of like what I was mentioning a little bit ago. If I'm really wrapped up in a project I love... I don't really notice that wound-up feeling. I try my very best to just focus and enjoy what I'm doing. 

I mean, I guess I couldn't say for one hundred percent certain if it completely, entirely goes away... maybe I'm still shifting my weight around or tapping a wrench on the workbench without realizing it? But I definitely don't feel that heavy motor running inside me like I do at a meeting. I just feel like I'm having a nice time and being useful. 

I hope I'm not just repeating myself too much! I'm sorry if I am. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for, Doctor. Did I answer that one okay for your notes?

When you're alone at home on a weekend with nothing you have to do and no particular plans—just free time—do you find yourself naturally wanting to get up and move around and do things, or can you comfortably sit and relax without that restless feeling pushing you to be active?

Oh, um... yes, I think it's a lot like what I was mentioning a few minutes ago. I hope you don't mind me repeating myself a little! I just want to make sure I'm being thorough for you. 

But yes, even if I have absolutely nothing scheduled on a Saturday, I don't really just sit in my chair and relax. It's exactly like how I am on my cleaning shifts—where I just keep moving right from mopping to checking the trash to straightening up the chairs. When I'm home with free time, I naturally just want to keep that momentum going. So instead of sitting down, I'll usually head right back out to the garage to putter around or find some tools to re-sort. 

I don't really think of it as a bad, restless feeling pushing me, though. I just... I like to be productive! I think it's a good thing to stay active and keep the house in order, don't you? I just want to be helpful. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope that answers your question the right way.
